steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The opening starts on a dissonant dominant seventh of F major — not the tonic C major — a deliberate subversion of Classical expectation. | Key Fact: The slow introduction (Adagio molto) delays the allegro, building anticipation before the first theme group enters in C major. | Key Fact: Beethoven's development section is unusually dramatic for a first symphony — he pushes harmonic and dynamic boundaries beyond Haydn's models. | Key Fact: The orchestration follows the Classical model but with Beethoven's characteristic weight: prominent winds, dynamic brass, and driving rhythmic energy.
